Tomato sauce is made by boiling fresh tomatoes and then straining them with various liquids until they are soft enough to be used as a condiment in food preparation. The resulting liquid (the tomato juice) is called tomato paste and it is then poured into jars containing either dried tomatoes or canned ones.

Keep a food diary
The first step in keeping up to date with your health is to keep a food diary. It can be very helpful when you feel like trying to maintain healthy weight, but it’s important to remember that even though you are living longer, there will be ups and downs along the way. Keeping track of what you eat and drink each day can help you stay on top of what’s going into your body over time. In fact, some studies have shown that keeping track of how much we get from our diet can help you avoid chronic diseases such as diabetes or heart disease.
2. Get a medical check-up
If you notice any changes in your symptoms or if you feel unsure about eating certain foods, get checked out by your doctor. You may want to see a dietitian who specializes in nutrition, especially if you take medication or just do some exercise, so they can better understand your needs and provide personalized advice. The most common problems for people with diabetes include high blood sugar levels, insulin resistance, or an increased need for insulin injections. Your doctor may recommend testing your blood glucose level every few months and making sure you don’t have too many tablets. This helps them know which medications are best for you. Kowalski has the opportunity to study corals at a depth of 10-25 meters in the Florida Keys, which is why she spends most of her time underwater.
“I’m fascinated by coral reefs,” says Kowalski, “because I believe that if we can understand their biology and help scientists learn how they work, then we will be able to better protect our oceans.”
When Dr. Kowalski was asked about coral reef research at UCSF, she replied:
“We’re just as concerned with restoring natural populations as we are about protecting human populations. We’ve done this for decades, but now it seems that we have lost the ability to manage ecosystems sustainably.”
The first step toward conservation was being able to determine whether a particular species of coral could survive and thrive under any conditions. To do so, Dr. Kowalski needed to know what kinds of corals were present on the islands, and what kind of habitat was available to them. She also had to know about the geology of these areas and the composition of those rocks, which she found challenging because they were so fragile. Dr. Kowalski was particularly interested in understanding the relationships between different types of coral reefs.
